messages.subject: defining post-stratification cluster size categories
parts:
Hi all

=20

Just a quick question about post-stratification by cluster size. Is
there an easy way to combine clusters into larger categories (i.e.
cluster sizes of between 1 and 4 into a single strata: '1-4') within
Distance, or do I need to add an extra field to the data which contains
the cluster size strata grouping? Since the number of observations in
each cluster size are likely to vary between surveys, the latter
approach will require quiet a lot more work in defining cluster size
strata and I am therefore keen to find a simpler approach within
Distance. Have looked through the manual and intro book and can find no
guidance on this.

=20

Cheers

Mark

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: defining post-stratification cluster size categories
parts:
Hi Mark, list,

If you want to stratify all components of estimation (detection function,
encounter rate, cluster size) by cluster size group, then you could either
do this by

- Post stratifying by cluster size group, as you indicate. In this case
you'll need a new field that defines the groupings, in the observation
layer. An example of this is the "Cluster strat" field in the Stratify
example sample project.

- Running a separate analysis for each cluster size group. For each
analysis you'd use a different data filter, and each data filter would use
the data selection tab to select out the range of cluster sizes that apply
to that group (e.g., [Cluster size]>=1 AND [Cluster size]<=3).

One of these days, I'm planning to add a "Formula" facility to the data
sheets in Distance, where the values of each row in a field are specified as
a combination of values for that row in other fields. Never seem to find
time for this sort of stuff...

Anyway, hope this helps,

- Len
